sections.title: Navigating Our Analytics Tools
sections.content: Our analytics suite provides powerful insights to help you understand player and team performance at a deeper level.

items.question: How do I find a specific player?
items.subtitle: Searching for player stats and analytics
items.answer: Navigate to Player Analytics and use the search bar at the top of the page. You can search by player name to instantly access their full statistical profile.

items.question: How do I view team statistics?
items.subtitle: Accessing comprehensive team data
items.answer: Go to Team Analytics and select any of the 30 MLB teams. You'll see:
list: Offensive statistics (runs, hits, home runs, OPS)

items.question: What statistics are available?
items.subtitle: Understanding the depth of our data
items.answer: We provide both traditional and advanced statistics including:
list: Traditional: AVG, HR, RBI, ERA, W-L

items.question: How often is the data updated?
items.subtitle: Staying current with the latest stats
items.answer: Our statistics are updated regularly throughout the MLB season to ensure you have access to the most current data for your analysis.

items.question: Can I compare multiple players or teams?
items.subtitle: Making side-by-side comparisons
items.answer: Yes! Our analytics tools allow you to compare performance metrics across different players and teams to identify trends and make informed decisions.

items.question: What if I don't understand a statistic?
items.subtitle: Learning baseball analytics terminology
items.answer: Visit our Glossary page for detailed explanations of all statistics and metrics used throughout the platform. Each term includes definitions and context for how to interpret the data.

sections.title: Understanding Baseball Analytics
sections.content: Get familiar with the key metrics and statistics we use to analyze player and team performance.

metrics.name: Batting Average (AVG)
metrics.description: Hits divided by at-bats. A fundamental measure of a hitter's ability to get on base via hits.

metrics.name: On-Base Plus Slugging (OPS)
metrics.description: Combines on-base percentage and slugging percentage. A comprehensive measure of hitting ability.

metrics.name: Earned Run Average (ERA)
metrics.description: Average earned runs allowed per nine innings pitched. Lower is better for pitchers.

metrics.name: Weighted On-Base Average (wOBA)
metrics.description: Advanced metric that weights each way of reaching base by its run value.

sections.title: Getting the Most From Our Analytics
sections.content: Tips and strategies for conducting effective baseball research using our platform.

tips.title: Start with the Basics
tips.description: Build your foundation before diving deep:
items: Familiarize yourself with traditional stats first
Use our Glossary to understand new metrics
Compare players within the same position group
Look at both recent performance and season-long trends

tips.title: Use Context
tips.description: Numbers tell a story, but context is key:
items: Consider ballpark factors when comparing players
Account for schedule difficulty and opponent quality
Look at splits (home/away, vs LHP/RHP) for deeper insights
Check for injuries or lineup changes that affect stats

tips.title: Identify Trends
tips.description: Look for patterns in the data:
items: Track recent form vs. season averages
Monitor hot and cold streaks
Compare performance across different time periods
Watch for breakout players or declining veterans

tips.title: Advanced Analysis
items: Use advanced metrics like wOBA and xFIP for better accuracy
Analyze matchup-specific data for head-to-head insights
Consider team-level stats alongside individual performance
Cross-reference multiple data points before drawing conclusions

sections.title: Research Reminder
sections.content: Baseball analytics provide valuable insights, but no statistic can predict the future with certainty. Use our tools as part of a comprehensive research approach, and always consider multiple factors when forming opinions about player and team performance.
